notes: No must-fix threat is identified inside the approved trusted-host, local-only, no-sensitive-data prototype boundary; independent review and M4 disposition remain required.
Remote access, sensitive data, untrusted callbacks, authenticity guarantees or hostile-host operation would expand the boundary and require new controls before use.

assumptions: The operator controls and protects the local host, checkout and output directories
Typed product inputs are untrusted data, while Python callbacks and operation identities are trusted declarations
Inputs contain no secrets or personal data unless a separately authorized confidentiality design is added
Synthetic fixtures establish software behavior and never establish physical-radio performance
scope.deployment: One authorized operator on one trusted local host using local files, loopback HTTP and synthetic or separately authorized data
excluded: Remote hosting, accounts, multi-user isolation, TLS and production service operation
Sandboxing arbitrary Python callbacks, general exactly-once external effects and hostile-host filesystem defense
Digital signatures, trusted time, build attestation, measurement authenticity, live hardware and certification
Handoff transport, receiver-host security and authenticity across an untrusted channel
included: Strict workflow, telemetry and fault-plan input boundaries
Durable execution, completed evidence, reports, handoff and read-only dashboard
Repository-level acceptance, performance and release evidence controls

controls.description: The declarative workflow accepts only bounded emit and fail operations and cannot name Python, shell, URL or adapter code.
The communications product path is a typed operator command with explicit input, output and no-overwrite contracts.

threats.impact: The callback can hang, mutate host state, access local data or bypass product evidence boundaries.
threats.preconditions: An untrusted party can select executable behavior or a trusted integrator supplies a hostile or defective callback.
threats.residual_risk: The public Python kernel still trusts in-process callbacks and has no sandbox, timeout or cancellation. Untrusted code execution is outside prototype scope.
threats.title: Untrusted code or callback gains host authority

controls.description: Strict schemas, duplicate-field rejection, exact units and byte, row, task and dependency bounds fail before use.
Reports, handoffs, completed artifacts and dashboard discovery use fixed allowlists and bounded reads or entry counts.

threats.impact: The operator can receive a false interpretation, excessive resource use or unavailable evidence.
threats.preconditions: A supplied workflow, telemetry file, report, workspace or archive is malformed, ambiguous or deliberately large.
threats.residual_risk: A trusted callback can still consume unbounded CPU, memory or I/O, and local disk exhaustion remains a host operational risk.
threats.title: Malformed or oversized input exhausts resources or changes meaning

controls.description: Canonical schemas, hashes and completed-run cross-validation reject disagreement among request, evidence, bindings, report and HTML.
The deterministic handoff reconstructs an exact allowlisted bundle from the immutable validated view and revalidates it on inspection.

threats.impact: Another engineer can investigate or hand off a result that did not originate from the claimed execution or measurement.
threats.preconditions: A party with write access alters one or more completed artifacts or replaces an entire unsigned evidence set.
threats.residual_risk: SHA-256 and cross-validation prove agreement, not authorship, trusted time, execution identity or measurement authenticity; coherent unsigned replacement remains possible.
threats.title: Evidence or report substitution creates a coherent false record

controls.description: Product and release controls refuse symbolic-link or existing output and use bounded regular-file reads and exclusive publication.
Linux journal ownership holds the database inode across callbacks and rejects aliases or changed paths at critical transitions.

threats.impact: Chimera can read unintended bytes, overwrite or expose local data, or associate evidence with the wrong durable state.
threats.preconditions: An untrusted same-host actor controls a directory or changes a path, inode, link or output name during operation.
threats.residual_risk: The prototype assumes trusted stable local directories and cooperative local processes; it is not hardened for hostile directory owners, every TOCTOU race or network filesystems.
threats.title: Path substitution, symbolic links or publication races redirect state

controls.description: Lifetime ownership, pre-callback running markers, pending-only resume and exact commit reconciliation fail closed to needs_attention.

threats.impact: A non-idempotent effect can be repeated, or incomplete work can be presented as completed evidence.
threats.preconditions: A process or commit fails around a callback whose external outcome is uncertain.
threats.residual_risk: Operation IDs are trusted declarations, uncooperative systems can bypass ownership, and ambiguous external effects require adapter-specific investigation rather than automatic exactly-once recovery.
threats.title: Interrupted work repeats an external side effect or is misreported complete

controls.description: The API and dashboard bind only to IPv4 loopback, expose GET-only immutable snapshots, enable no CORS and return restrictive headers.
Report and dashboard HTML escape untrusted text, remain script-free and use restrictive content and framing policies.

threats.impact: Local evidence can be disclosed, an audit interface can weaken evidence integrity, or crafted text can mislead an operator or execute active browser content.
threats.preconditions: Another same-host process can connect to loopback, the operator treats presentation as mutation authority, or crafted evidence text reaches rendered HTML.
threats.residual_risk: Loopback is not authentication or confidentiality from other same-host processes; there is no TLS, account, authorization or hostile-host isolation, and future templates require the same escaping discipline.
threats.title: Loopback presentation discloses, mutates or injects rendered evidence

controls.description: Inspection admits the exact six-entry order and allowlist, stored unencrypted bytes, bounded sizes and a complete cross-validated reopened run.

threats.impact: Archive processing can expose the host or accept evidence outside the declared portable artifact set.
threats.preconditions: An operator inspects a crafted, changed, oversized or path-bearing ZIP archive.
threats.residual_risk: Archive integrity is unsigned and local temporary/output directory trust still applies; handoffs over untrusted channels need a separately authorized authenticity design.
threats.title: A malicious handoff archive writes or validates unintended content

controls.description: The manual prohibits secrets and personal data, while the approved dashboard remains local, read-only and no-cache.

threats.impact: Sensitive bytes can persist in JSON, SQLite, reports, archives or loopback responses without redaction or encryption.
threats.preconditions: An operator supplies sensitive task values, error text or telemetry despite the declared no-sensitive-data assumption.
threats.residual_risk: Chimera has no automatic redaction, encryption at rest, access control or confidentiality guarantee. Sensitive-data use requires a scope and threat-model change before release use.
threats.title: Secrets or personal data persist in evidence and local responses

controls.description: CI uses read-only permissions, no persisted checkout credential, bounded jobs, exact official Action pins and no deployment step.
The isolated wheel check proves installation and runtime dependency shape outside the source checkout.

threats.impact: Hosted evidence or built artifacts can differ from reviewed source without an authenticated, reproducible build chain.
threats.preconditions: A runner image, package index, build tool, browser package or operating-system dependency changes or is compromised.
threats.residual_risk: Hosted runners, ranged build tools, PyPI, Chromium and system packages remain mutable; no signed artifact, SBOM or trusted build attestation is claimed.
threats.title: Mutable CI or dependency inputs produce untrusted release evidence

controls.description: Acceptance preparation is exact-candidate bound and always leaves every human observation and phase disposition blank or pending.
Performance evidence is explicitly synthetic and excludes hardware, capacity, browser, HTTP and service-level claims.

threats.impact: A phase or release can appear accepted without the required human observation or valid engineering evidence.
threats.preconditions: A test, benchmark, blank worksheet or synthetic result is described as operator approval, product acceptance or physical-system validation.
threats.residual_risk: Automation cannot perform Leo's walkthrough, accept residual risk, approve M4/M5 or establish measurement authenticity; those decisions remain pending.
threats.title: Automated or synthetic evidence is misrepresented as human or physical acceptance
